content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Bremerton

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a specific combination of formal education and project-management experience before you apply. Review PMI's eligibility criteria—which account for your academic background and hours leading projects—to confirm you meet the baseline. Granite PM Academy's enrollment team can help clarify whether your background qualifies.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp and attend all instructor-led sessions. Our nationwide schedule accommodates working professionals in Bremerton; you'll join from your location and learn project-management frameworks, processes, and best practices directly from active certified practitioners over the full course.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the 35-hour course, create your PMI account and complete the official PMP application. You'll document your project experience and education, then submit your application and exam fee directly to PMI for review and approval before your exam eligibility window opens.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Once PMI approves your application, use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, study guides, and practice exams to build confidence. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner at your preferred test center and sit for the PMP® exam on your timeline.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: The PMP® credential remains valid for three years. Earn professional development units (PDUs) through training, volunteer work, or project experience during each three-year cycle to renew your certification. Granite PM Academy offers ongoing PDU-eligible courses to support your continuing education and career growth.
